title: 5G NR LDPC base graphs and per-i_LS shift tables (BG1+BG2, key rates)
description:
## Goal

Land / complete the 3GPP TS 38.212 LDPC base graphs (BG1, BG2) and the
per-`i_LS` shift tables for all 8 lifting sets covering rates {1/3, 1/2,
2/3, 5/6}, verified **bit-exact vs external 3GPP reference test
vectors**.

## Context

Task under story `a5635da5` (5G NR + research enablers) within epic
`gf2-sim` (`f9717e7e`). Per-`i_LS` correctness is a known trap
(`feedback_ldpc_shift_tables`: single lifting-set tables cause ~2 dB
BLER loss).

**AMENDMENT 2026-06-09 (user-approved scope correction — NO rigor
change; correctness criteria KEPT/STRENGTHENED).** A read of the
codebase shows 5G NR LDPC is ALREADY substantially built in
`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/` (`bg1.rs`, `bg2.rs`, `lifting.rs`,
`mod.rs`): `LIFTING_SIZE_SETS` is a per-`i_LS` table indexed 0..7,
`bg1_base_matrix(z)`/`bg2_base_matrix(z)` already apply the `V mod Z`
shifts (host-side, matching the flat-kernel architecture), and
`QuasiCyclicLdpc::nr_5g(...)` + ~53 unit tests exist. So this task's
real residual is (a) COVERAGE completion (all 8 sets × the 4 rates if
any are missing) and (b) the genuinely-missing **external reference-
vector validation** — the existing tests are SELF-CONSISTENCY
roundtrips, NOT validated against 3GPP/aff3ct reference vectors. The
deliverables are re-scoped to the REAL API surface (the named
`BaseGraph`/`ShiftTable`/`LiftingSet`/`NrRate` types and the
`bg1_shifts.toml`/`bg2_shifts.toml` files do NOT exist — the real
surface is `QuasiCyclicLdpc::nr_5g` + the free functions
`all_lifting_sizes`/`lifting_set_index`/`is_valid_lifting_size`, and
the shift tables are compiled-in Rust consts). All `[hard]` correctness
criteria are KEPT (and the external-vector criterion is the rigorous
new bar).

## Deliverables

1. Audit + completion of `crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/nr_5g/`:
   - BG1 base graph per TS 38.212 §5.3.2 Table 5.3.2-2; BG2 per Table
     5.3.2-3; per-`i_LS` `V` shift tables for all 8 lifting sets;
     lifting-size-set enumeration (Table 5.3.2-1). Confirm coverage of
     rates {1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6} and fill any gaps. (`i_LS` is derived
     from `Z` via `lifting_set_index`, not passed separately.)
2. **External reference-vector validation (the rigorous residual):**
   - Add bit-exact regression tests validating BG1/BG2 + per-`i_LS`
     shifts against an EXTERNAL reference (3GPP TS 38.212 sample data
     or aff3ct's 5G NR LDPC vectors) — one regression per (BG, `i_LS`,
     `Z`, rate) in scope. Tag tests that require fetched vector files
     `#[ignore = "external: ..."]` and `sim`/`slow` as needed to stay
     under the fast-tier 5 s cap. If a usable external reference is
     genuinely unobtainable, ESCALATE (blocker) — do NOT downgrade to a
     self-consistency check.
3. Public API on `gf2_coding::ldpc::nr_5g`:
   - Audit/EXTEND the EXISTING surface (`QuasiCyclicLdpc::nr_5g` + the
     free functions) so callers can construct a valid base graph for any
     in-scope (BG, lifting set, rate) tuple. Add constructors/wrappers
     as needed; do NOT assume the `BaseGraph::bg1(rate, i_LS, z)` /
     `ShiftTable` / `NrRate` names exist verbatim (re-scoped per the
     2026-06-09 amendment).
4. Shift-table representation: the per-`i_LS` tables exist as compiled-in
   Rust consts in `bg1.rs`/`bg2.rs`. Externalising them to
   `data/ldpc/nr_5g/bg{1,2}_shifts.toml` is OPTIONAL (a representation
   choice, not a correctness requirement) — only do it if it improves
   maintainability; the consts are an acceptable SSOT.
5. CLAUDE.md note pointing to the `nr_5g` module in the gf2-coding
   module map (folded into the Phase E close at `110e45cc`; this task
   contributes the diff).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] BG1 + BG2 + per-`i_LS` shift tables for all 8 lifting sets and
  rates {1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6} present and verified **bit-exact against
  EXTERNAL TS 38.212 / aff3ct reference test vectors** — one regression
  per (BG, `i_LS`, `Z`, rate). (Self-consistency roundtrips do NOT
  satisfy this; the external reference is the bar.)
- [hard] Per-`i_LS` indexing tested explicitly: a regression forcing the
  WRONG `i_LS` table for a given `Z` yields a test failure (the ~2 dB
  trap guard).
- [hard] The public `gf2_coding::ldpc::nr_5g` surface constructs valid
  base graphs for any in-scope (BG, lifting set, rate) tuple (built on
  the existing `QuasiCyclicLdpc::nr_5g` surface per the amendment).
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review`, `tests` gates green.

## Non-goals

- GPU kernel tuning (owned by `23d3525f`).
- Encoder GPU offload (epic non-goal).
- Rate matching, HARQ buffer (out of scope; epic is LDPC core only).

## AMENDMENT 2026-06-12 (user-approved): per-BG rate scope

Criterion 1's rate set {1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6} applies per base graph
WITHIN TS 38.212's operating region: BG1 x {1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6} and
BG2 x {1/3, 1/2, 2/3}. 3GPP TS 38.212 clause 7.2.2 selects BG2 only
for rates R <= 0.67 (BG2's design region); BG2 at 5/6 is outside the
standard and is NOT required. No rigor change: the per-`i_LS` shift
tables are verified bit-exact for BOTH base graphs across all 8
lifting sets and every valid Z (the rate dimension does not affect
the tables; it enters only via the constructor-surface coverage).
The exclusion is cited in `tests/nr5g_external_vectors.rs`'s module
header.
